counterexample:
Take k = 2 and any ring R in which q(q+1) is invertible (e.g. R = Q, q = 2), and let dim V = 5 = 2k+1, b an ordered basis. With the modified definition of line 0426, for a 2-dimensional W one has c_{b,W} = d|_{W_b}(q^{-2}(W - c_{b,partial W})), and running the induction of Prop "Cone Identity" gives

  partial c_{b,W} = (W - c_{b,partial W}) + q^{-2} d|_{W_b}( c_{b, partial^2 W} ).

Here partial^2 W = (q+1) * 0 (the zero space with coefficient q+1, by Claim delta squared), so c_{b,partial^2 W} = (q+1) Span{b_1} and the residual term is q^{-2}(q+1) * (sum of all 2-dimensional subspaces of W_b containing b_1), a sum of binom(4,1)_q distinct basis chains with the nonzero coefficient q^{-2}(q+1). It is therefore not zero, so the cone identity partial c_{b,W} = W - c_{b,partial W} fails, and consequently (i) the chain W - c_{b,partial W} is not in Ker(partial_2) (its boundary is c_{b,partial^2 W} != 0) and (ii) the identity alpha = partial c_{b,alpha} used at line 0431 is unavailable. Independently, the stated hypothesis is already insufficient: for R = Z and q = 2, "q is not zero in R" holds but q^{-k} does not exist in R, so the definition at line 0426 is not even well posed.

CONCLUSION: everything up to and including Theorem "homologies vanish middle", the expansion theorem, the cone-size bound, the eta_n/psi_n constructions and Claim partdom checks out (modulo many typos). The proof of Proposition "small generators" (the claimed resolution of the Mnukhin-Siemons projective support dimension conjecture) fails at line 0424: it asserts the cone machinery carries over to rings where q is nonzero, but (a) it needs q invertible, not merely nonzero/not dividing the characteristic, and (b) in precisely that regime partial^2 != 0 (Claim delta squared), while the cone identity was proved using partial^2 = 0. Hence VERDICT: INVALID, first failing step 0424.
